column3: NASB adds “in this manner.”
NASB follows the critical text (“In this case”); “faithful” is rendered “trustworthy.”
NASB renders “the smallest matter” as “a very small thing” and adds “any.”
NASB renders “have I been justified” as “am I … acquitted” and “judging” as “examines.”
NASB adds “go on” and “but wait,” renders “of darkness” as “in the darkness,” and adds “men's.”
NASB follows the critical text without “to think”; it renders “applied” as “figuratively applied” and “be puffed up” as “become arrogant.”
NASB renders “makes you different” as “regards you as superior.”
NASB renders “satiated” as “filled” and “reigned” as “become kings.”
NASB follows the critical text without “that”; “appointed to death” is rendered “men condemned to death,” and it adds “of all.”
NASB renders “wise” as “prudent” and “honored” as “distinguished.”
NASB renders “are buffeted” as “are roughly treated” and “wander homeless” as “are homeless.”
NASB adds “when.”
NASB follows the critical text (“slandered”); “we entreat” is rendered “we try to conciliate,” and “refuse” is “dregs.”
NASB follows the critical text; the participle is rendered “to admonish.”
NASB renders “ten thousand” as “countless,” “guardians” as “tutors,” and “I begot you” as “I became your father.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB has “in Christ” without “Jesus,” following other manuscripts; it adds “and he.”
NASB renders “were puffed up” as “have become arrogant” and reorders the verse.
NASB renders “talk” as “words” and adds “their.”
NASB renders “is not in word” as “does not consist in words.”
Close to the Greek.
